hook: "A new EU law is about to change how AI-generated content can be used in ads and if you're running AI UGC, this affects you."
body: A regulatory warning: from August 2, 2026 the EU AI Act (Article 50) requires AI-generated content to be labeled (machine-readable), splitting "fully AI-generated" vs "AI-assisted" disclosure, with fines up to €15M or 3% of global turnover. The sting for AI UGC: its whole appeal is looking like real organic customer content — exactly the blurred line the law targets.
cta: Implicit: reconsider AI UGC or move to traditional organic creation; hashtags for reach.
idea: The EU AI Act's disclosure rules directly attack AI UGC's core advantage (indistinguishability from real customer content).
sequencing: Alarm: new EU law changes AI content in ads.
The rule: Article 50, labeling from Aug 2 2026, fully-AI vs AI-assisted split.
The penalty: €15M or 3% of turnover.
The sting: AI UGC's appeal IS the blurred line.
The pivot: traditional organic creation or watch CPAs "sky dive."
formatting: Long text explainer post with legal specifics; hashtag block at the end.
why_it_works: A dated legal deadline + a huge fine number + a direct threat to the reader's current tactic creates urgency no creative tip can match.
what_to_steal: The compliance heads-up for LC's AI-dupe program: build the disclosure workflow (AI-assisted vs fully-AI labeling) into the pipeline now, before the August deadline forces a scramble.

body: A lead-magnet post giving away a complete AI-UGC system: $74k/mo claimed from AI UGC avatars, 300+ creatives tested across 40 products, no creators hired, no products shipped. The attached 27s demo video (transcript in file) is an AI avatar selling swimwear: "I do not want tiny bikini bottoms. I want something I can actually swim in without checking myself every 10 seconds."
cta: RT + comment "scale" (must follow for DM) to receive the full system.
idea: AI avatars can run a full native-looking UGC creative system — no creators, no shoots — and every winning hook can be re-varied in minutes.
sequencing: Hook: $74k/mo from AI UGC.
The system: no creators, no shipping, no filming, no reshoots.
Proof: 300+ creatives, 40 products, the exact realism setup.
Demo: the 27s swimwear AI-avatar video.
The giveaway list: scripts, prompts, 100 variations/week, hook framework.
Gate: RT + comment "scale" + follow.
formatting: Long lead-magnet thread + 27s AI-avatar demo video (video.twimg.com). Checklist of what's inside the giveaway.
why_it_works: The "no" list (no creators, no products, no filming, no reshoots, no waiting) sells the absence of pain, and the live demo video proves the claim in the same scroll.
what_to_steal: The demo-video structure for LC: a 27s AI avatar delivering ONE relatable complaint + product answer ("I don't want jewelry that turns my skin green…") — native, fast, infinitely re-skinable.

product: commentary — no product (landing-page playbook; sleep-gummies example)
hook: "Google Ads funnels are one of the biggest untapped opportunities in eCom right now."
body: A landing-page playbook for Google Ads funnels: above the fold = headline mirroring the query + outcome-with-timeframe subhead + result-showing hero image + ONE value-stating CTA. Below the fold sequences differ by traffic type: short for transactional (trust bar → benefits → social proof → details → FAQ → CTA), long editorial for informational (agitate with Reddit language → why alternatives fail → mechanism → proof → comparison → guarantee → CTA), medium for comparison. The #1 mistake: sending every campaign to the same PDP.
idea: Message match is everything: build angle-specific landing pages per campaign instead of one generic PDP, and the above-the-fold has exactly four elements.
sequencing: Hook: GADs funnels are untapped.
Above the fold: 4 elements, one job (confirm the click).
Headline mirrors the query; subhead states outcome + timeframe.
Hero shows the RESULT, not the product; one value-stating CTA.
Below-fold sequences for transactional / informational / comparison traffic.
The #1 mistake: one PDP for every campaign.
Proof claim: 2-3x conversion for angle-specific pages.
CTA: DM for a walkthrough.
formatting: Very long educational thread with nested blockquotes; one photo. Consultant authority voice.
why_it_works: A rigid checklist ("4 elements. No more.") plus a named #1 mistake gives the reader both the system and the sin to confess, which drives DMs.
what_to_steal: The above-the-fold 4-element formula and the "result, not product" hero rule for LC's advertorials — plus the discipline of angle-specific landers for each major LC ad angle (tarnish, gifting, stacking).

hook: "If you ever run out of things to post on Instagram, save this."
body: A giant organic content idea bank: 30+ reel formats, 20+ carousel formats, 25+ static formats, 25+ story formats — plus a repurposing doctrine (one case study → reel, carousel, static, story, LinkedIn, X, email). Includes UGC-style/customer-POV videos and customer photos as explicit line items.
idea: Content volume is a format problem, not an ideas problem: one idea becomes seven posts across formats.
sequencing: Hook: the save prompt.
Reels: 30+ formats (tutorials → storytelling → challenges).
Carousels: 20+ formats (guides → myths vs facts → FAQs).
Statics: 25+ formats (testimonials → customer photo → UGC).
Stories: 25+ formats (polls → reviews → countdowns).
Repurposing: one idea, seven formats.
The series trick: one format, many industries.
formatting: Very long categorized list post. Save-worthy reference format.
why_it_works: Exhaustiveness is the value: the reader saves it because it replaces "what do I post" anxiety with a menu they'll never finish.
what_to_steal: The repurposing doctrine for LC: every winning jewelry concept ships as reel + carousel + static + story on day one — and the "customer photo / UGC / testimonial" line items as standing weekly slots in the content calendar.
